scenes.title: One heap, two views
scenes.description: Follow a new value through a min-heap with linked array blocks and a binary tree.
scenes.markdown:
# Algorithm Structures

## Insert 5 into a min-heap

A min-heap is a **complete binary tree** whose parent is never larger than either child. The array and tree below are **two views of the same objects**. Colors travel with the objects; array indices stay put.

Use **Execution state** to visit any of the seven states, forwards or backwards. Hover a block in either view to illuminate its partner. Click to keep that object selected; click empty space to clear.

**0 · Ready** — the six existing values already satisfy the heap rule.

**1 · Append** — place 5 in the next free array slot, index 6. This preserves the complete tree shape.

**2 · Compare** — compare 5 with its parent, 10. For zero-based indexing, `p = floor((i − 1) / 2)`.

**3 · Swap** — 5 moves up to index 2, while 10 moves down. Only the path to the root can need repair.

**4 · Compare** — now compare 5 with 8 at the root.

**5 · Swap** — 5 reaches index 0.

**6 · Done** — the heap rule holds again. A heap is only partially ordered: siblings need not be sorted.

The scalar variables **key** and **n** hold numbers. **i** and **p** explicitly reference cells of array **A**; their arrows follow those cells. At the root there is no parent reference.

Try jumping from state 0 to 5, then back to 2. Which objects move? Which parent relationships change? In a tree of height h, insertion makes at most h upward swaps: O(log n).

## Free-play controls

Edit **Starting min-heap A** in the slider panel and change **Insert key**. The starting six values must satisfy the min-heap rule; an invalid edit displays an explanation. Try key **25** (no swaps), **9** (one swap), and **5** (two swaps). Equal values keep separate identities and do not swap.

**Execution state** selects a snapshot directly. The caption shows the actual state count; positions beyond a shorter run select its final state. **Movement seconds** controls the transition, with 0 for instant jumps. **Block depth** changes the relief. Drag to orbit, or choose **Front** / **Toy blocks**. The numbered walkthrough above describes the default inputs.
